source: Public companion canon build — Known Descent boundary enforced
hornRule: At 1200 hours (day 50 of the 2400-hour Opening), a giant horn sounds throughout the Decennium — the point of no return. Adventurers must retreat or risk being trapped in the depths for 10 years until the next Cycle. Soft quit at Floor 50 Canticle is separate from the Horn.

cycle.calendar: 400-day year, 10 months of 40 days; Holyday on the 10th of each month; final 10 days = Twilight Week when divine and mortal boundaries blur.
cycle.rotation: 10-year rotation — the Shardspire activates in the tenth year. Cycles are named after their victor.

entryClasses.directorNote: Current Director baseline: no player-facing rule restricts Cycle entry by class. All 17 selectable base classes may attempt entry unless a campaign-specific rule states otherwise.
entryClasses.policy: All 17 canon classes may attempt entry when the Shardspire activates; the Great Descent does not bar entry by class. Fighter/Swashbuckler are legacy aliases only and are not selectable base classes.

victoryConsequences.directorNote: Director default, 2026-07-29 overnight — draft flavor consequences derived from each tier's boss/zone theme in floor-encounters.json, in the spirit of the rulebook's 'new laws, weather, or rulers based on the god favored by the victor' line and the existing mythHistory entries below. Not mechanical rules; author/Continuity review before treating as canon.
victoryConsequences.summary: Recognized Cycle honors and economic consequences are recorded only for depths that expeditions have actually cleared and returned from.

byTier.consequence: Automaton labor charters and cavern mining rights are reopened or revoked at the victor's word; crystal-light guilds gain a seat at court.
Quarantine and foraging law reform; druidic and swamp-warden circles gain jurisdiction over marsh territories; hunger-cult purges or protections follow depending on the victor's temperament.
Brogi's forge-priesthood is elevated to state smiths; new weapon-tax and fire-safety edicts are issued in the victor's name.
Calendar and liturgical reform around the radiant sects; 'Architect' cults are either declared orthodox or outlawed depending on the victor's alignment.
A Choir doctrine schism or unification follows; new liturgical law on public silence/song; the Bar of Last Refuge becomes a formal pilgrimage waypoint.

mythHistory: The Age of Dawns: When the First Light split, the world was shaped by the Tenfold Truths. The continents formed from divine clashes. Rivers ran where Velkyrion’s blade cut mountains. Forests grew where Kharix fell in grief.

The Prohibition Beneath the Descent: late temple copies disagree about what was sealed, where it was sealed, and whether the event occurred at all. Tier IV expeditions report recurring warning symbols, but no accepted source identifies their subject.
The First Cycle: The Shardspire glowed, and mortals entered. A farmer emerged with a crown of flame, founding Tyrnathar. The advent of divine war through mortals began.
The Sundering of the Beastlands: When Threxian's forces cut through the Thauren Expanse, Kharix retaliated with living storms. Half the tribes were lost. Terhakor was born in the aftermath.
The Betrayal of the Veil: Yshael, once an ally to Elyria, tricked her into transferring a third of her power into a relic. This relic vanished into the dungeon, altering its structure permanently.

expedition.summary: Expeditions distribute up to 12 characters across combat, reconnaissance, research, resource, and support activities — not every member delves at once.
